message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they diverged from other carnivores early on. Their lineage split from the ursid (bear) family around 20–25 million years ago. Fossil evidence shows that the giant panda’s ancestors were omnivorous, with teeth adapted for both meat and plant matter. Over time, the giant panda evolved a specialized bamboo diet, developing strong jaws and a pseudo-thumb for grasping bamboo stalks. The red panda, though sharing the name, belongs to its own separate family (Ailuridae) and diverged from other carnivorans earlier, around 40–50 million years ago. Both lineages have undergone adaptations to their respective environments, leading to the distinct species we see today.
